title: Trump Returns to White House Correspondents' Dinner Three Months After Assassination Attempt
excerpt: The rescheduled event moves to a smaller venue with heightened security after a gunman stormed the April gala, forcing evacuations and leaving a Secret Service officer wounded.
body:
• President Trump delivered remarks at a rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner at the Waldorf Astoria on Friday, three months after the April event was cut short by a shooting.
  • The guest list shrank from 2,600 to roughly 680, with airport-style screening, QR-coded entry and a single access point through a private entrance.
  • WHCA President Weijia Jiang honored Secret Service Officer Victor Gonzales, who was wounded intercepting suspect Cole Tomas Allen in April.
  • Trump criticized late-night hosts and some reporters during a 30-minute speech, while more than 500 journalists had urged the WHCA to publicly defend press freedom.

A Defiant Return

President Donald Trump took the stage Friday evening at the Waldorf Astoria in Washington to finish the speech he never got to deliver in April. The original White House Correspondents' Dinner at the Washington Hilton ended abruptly when an armed suspect, Cole Tomas Allen, breached security and allegedly attempted to assassinate the president, triggering an evacuation of hundreds of journalists and administration officials.

https://x.com/WhiteHouse/status/2080813430227759120

Allen was tackled by Secret Service agents one floor above the ballroom after an exchange of gunfire that left officer Victor Gonzales wounded. He has since been charged with attempting to assassinate the president and assaulting a federal officer with a deadly weapon.

Smaller Venue, Tighter Security

The rescheduled dinner traded the Hilton's sprawling ballroom for the Waldorf Astoria's more intimate space — roughly half the size. The guest list was cut from 2,600 to about 680. Organizers worked with the Secret Service and a private security firm to redesign the event's security architecture. Every pre-vetted guest received a unique QR code, had to present government-issued identification, and passed through airport-style screening at the venue's single access point.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Vr7cd26PbNw

WHCA President Weijia Jiang, a CBS News correspondent, said the changes were necessary to close the gaps exposed during the April attack. "I do feel very good about the measures that we've taken and really thought through," she told People magazine.

Press Freedom and Political Barbs

Trump opened with remarks about the First Amendment and thanked Secret Service officers for their actions in April. He then pivoted to a freewheeling 30-minute address targeting political enemies, comedians Jimmy Kimmel, Jimmy Fallon and Stephen Colbert — whom he called "sick people" — and CNN's Kaitlan Collins, whom he described as "nasty."

The speech came amid heightened tensions between the White House and the press corps. More than 500 journalists had signed a letter urging the WHCA to publicly criticize Trump's attacks on press freedom during the event.

"We will not allow an act of violence to have the last words, especially during a year when we are reflecting on the 250th anniversary of America and everything we stand for."

— Weijia Jiang, WHCA President

Who Was There — and Who Wasn't

The evening honored Officer Gonzales with the WHCA's President's Award for Exceptional Service. Journalists recognized included New York Times reporter Tyler Pager, whose award came one day after the Justice Department withdrew subpoenas seeking information about his sources.

First Lady Melania Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio did not attend, citing scheduling conflicts. War Secretary Pete Hegseth, FBI Director Kash Patel and acting Attorney General Todd Blanche were among the officials present.
nri_angle: The rescheduled dinner underscored First Amendment protections and press freedom debates relevant to all Americans, including Indian Americans working in media and politics.
